% Phase 4 (Héctor Armenteros): Probabilities and System Size N = 100 + M (Part 2 a–d).
% All numerical values generated by src/thermodynamics.py (python -m src.thermodynamics).

\subsection{Probabilities and Macrostate Intervals for $N = 100 + M$}

\paragraph{Determination of system size $N = 100 + M$.}
The group size parameter $M$ is defined as the harmonic average of the last two digits of each team member's NIA:
\begin{itemize}
    \item Guillermo García Pelayo: 69
    \item Andrés Mármol del Amo: 22
    \item Héctor Armenteros Arauzo: 09 (treated as 9)
    \item Carlos Cordero López: 45
\end{itemize}
The harmonic mean is calculated as:
\begin{equation}
    M = \frac{n}{\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{x_i}} = \frac{4}{\frac{1}{69} + \frac{1}{22} + \frac{1}{9} + \frac{1}{45}} \approx \frac{4}{0.193281} \approx 20.6953.
\end{equation}
Following standard rounding to the nearest integer, we obtain $M = 21$, yielding a system size of:
\begin{equation}
    N = 100 + M = 121 \quad \text{coins}.
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Handling of odd $N$.}
Because $N = 121$ is an odd integer, the mathematical midpoint $N/2 = 60.5$ is a half-integer. Since a physical macrostate corresponds to an integer number of heads $k \in \{0, 1, \dots, N\}$, the probability distribution exhibits two degenerate, symmetrically equivalent modal peaks at:
\begin{equation}
    k_{\text{peak}} = \left\lfloor \frac{N}{2} \right\rfloor = 60 \quad \text{and} \quad k_{\text{peak}} = \left\lceil \frac{N}{2} \right\rceil = 61.
\end{equation}
By binomial symmetry, $\Omega(121, 60) = \Omega(121, 61)$, so both macrostates possess identical multiplicity and probability.

\paragraph{Log-space computation.}
Probabilities are evaluated in log space to prevent numerical overflow or underflow:
\begin{equation}
    P(N, k) = \frac{\Omega(N, k)}{2^N} = \exp\left( \ln\Omega(N, k) - N\ln 2 \right),
\end{equation}
where $\ln\Omega(N, k) = \ln\Gamma(N+1) - \ln\Gamma(k+1) - \ln\Gamma(N-k+1)$ is evaluated via \texttt{math.lgamma}. All values below were computed using \texttt{src/thermodynamics.py} and verified through unit tests in \texttt{tests/test\_thermodynamics.py}.

\paragraph{(a) Probability of $k = 30$ heads.}
For $k = 30$ heads out of $N = 121$ coins:
\begin{equation}
    P(121, 30) = 8.490094 \times 10^{-9}.
\end{equation}
This state lies $5.55\sigma$ away from the mean (with $\sigma = \sqrt{N}/2 = 5.50$ coins). Its probability is less than 1 in 100 million, illustrating how rapidly the binomial tail vanishes away from the center.

\paragraph{(b) Probability of the most probable macrostate ($k = N/2$).}
At the degenerate peak macrostates $k = 60$ and $k = 61$:
\begin{equation}
    P(121, 60) = P(121, 61) = 0.072089 \quad (7.21\,\%).
\end{equation}
The multiplicity of each peak is $\Omega(121, 60) \approx 1.916167 \times 10^{35}$ microstates. The probability that the system is found in either of these two most probable macrostates is $P(60) + P(61) = 0.144179$ ($14.42\,\%$).

\paragraph{(c) Interval probability $\Delta P$ for heads around the mean ($k \in [N/2 - 10, N/2 + 10]$).}
The continuous symmetric interval $[60.5 - 10, 60.5 + 10] = [50.5, 70.5]$ covers the 20 integer macrostates $k \in [51, 70]$. Summing the probabilities yields:
\begin{equation}
    \Delta P_{\text{heads}} = \sum_{k=51}^{70} P(121, k) = 0.931406 \quad (93.14\,\%).
\end{equation}
If evaluated centered on the integer mode $k = 60$, the 21 macrostates in $[50, 70]$ give $\Delta P = 0.943177$ ($94.32\,\%$), and including both symmetric boundaries $[50, 71]$ (22 states) gives $\Delta P = 0.954948$ ($95.49\,\%$). Thus, a band spanning only $16.4\,\%$ of the macrostates concentrates over $93\,\%$ of the total probability mass.

\paragraph{(d) Interval probability $\Delta P$ for tails around the mean ($t \in [N/2 - 20, N/2 + 20]$).}
The number of tails in any microstate is $t = N - k$. Because fair coin tossing is symmetric with respect to heads and tails ($p = q = 1/2$), the probability distribution is strictly invariant under the exchange of heads and tails:
\begin{equation}
    P_{\text{tails}}(N, t) = P_{\text{heads}}(N, t).
\end{equation}
The symmetric interval of tails $t \in [50.5 - 20, 50.5 + 20] = [40.5, 80.5]$ encompasses the integer range $t \in [41, 80]$. In terms of heads, this corresponds to $41 \le 121 - k \le 80 \iff 41 \le k \le 80$. The cumulative probability is:
\begin{equation}
    \Delta P_{\text{tails}} = \sum_{t=41}^{80} P(121, t) = 0.999756 \quad (99.9756\,\%).
\end{equation}
Around the integer mode $[40, 80]$, $\Delta P = 0.999820$ ($99.982\,\%$). This width corresponds to $\pm 20/\sigma \approx \pm 3.64$ standard deviations, rendering the probability of observing a system outside this window less than $0.025\,\%$.
